items.followUp: What happens to the DNA and chromosome number during the S-phase of interphase?

rubric.why: The key event in S-phase is DNA replication, resulting in duplicated chromosomes.
rubric.description: DNA replicates, forming two sister chromatids for each chromosome.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that DNA is replicated or duplicated and that chromosomes form two sister chromatids.

rubric.why: S-phase doubles the DNA content but does not change the chromosome number.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that chromosome number stays the same.

modelAnswer: During S-phase, DNA replicates and each chromosome forms two sister chromatids.
The DNA content doubles, but the chromosome number remains unchanged.

items.followUp: Define synapsis and state during which stage of meiosis it occurs.

rubric.why: Synapsis is the pairing of homologous chromosomes.
rubric.description: Homologous chromosomes pair with each other.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing the pairing or coming together of homologous chromosomes.

rubric.why: Synapsis occurs during prophase I, specifically in zygotene.
rubric.description: It occurs in prophase I of meiosis (zygotene).
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying prophase I or zygotene.

modelAnswer: Synapsis is the pairing of homologous chromosomes.
It occurs during prophase I of meiosis, specifically in zygotene.

items.followUp: What is the effect of an unsuitable temperature on an enzyme?

rubric.why: Denaturation alters the enzyme's structure, including the shape of its active site.
rubric.description: Denaturation changes the enzyme's structure or the shape of its active site.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the enzyme's shape or structure, particularly its active site, changes.

rubric.why: A changed active site prevents the enzyme from catalysing its reaction normally.
rubric.description: The enzyme loses its catalytic activity.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the denatured enzyme loses its activity or can no longer catalyse the reaction.

modelAnswer: Denaturation is a change in an enzyme's structure that alters the shape of its active site.
As a result, the enzyme loses its catalytic activity.

items.followUp: Differentiate between a cofactor and a coenzyme.

rubric.why: A prosthetic group is the non-protein component firmly attached to an enzyme.
rubric.description: A prosthetic group is tightly or permanently bound to its enzyme.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing the prosthetic group as tightly or permanently bound.

rubric.why: A coenzyme associates less firmly and can separate from the enzyme.
rubric.description: A coenzyme is loosely or temporarily attached and can dissociate.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing the coenzyme as loosely or temporarily bound, or able to dissociate.

modelAnswer: A prosthetic group is a non-protein component that is tightly or permanently bound to an enzyme.
A coenzyme is an organic non-protein component that is loosely bound and can dissociate from the enzyme.

items.followUp: Define metabolism and name the two main types of metabolic reactions.

rubric.why: Bioenergetics concerns energy relationships and transformations in living organisms.
rubric.description: Bioenergetics is the study of energy relationships or transformations in living organisms.
rubric.how: Award 2 marks for defining bioenergetics as the study of energy relationships or transformations in living organisms.

modelAnswer: Bioenergetics is the study of energy relationships and energy transformations in living organisms.

items.followUp: Name four factors that can limit the rate of photosynthesis.

rubric.why: Light intensity, carbon dioxide concentration, temperature, and water availability are limiting factors for photosynthesis; chlorophyll is also an accepted factor.
rubric.description: Four limiting factors affecting photosynthesis are listed.
rubric.how: Award 2 marks for listing any four of light intensity, carbon dioxide concentration, temperature, water availability, and chlorophyll.

modelAnswer: Four limiting factors of photosynthesis are light intensity, carbon dioxide concentration, temperature, and water availability.

items.followUp: Write the equation for lactic acid fermentation and state where it occurs.

rubric.why: Alcoholic fermentation is the anaerobic breakdown of glucose, commonly by yeast, producing ethanol and carbon dioxide.
rubric.description: Glucose is broken down without oxygen to form ethanol and carbon dioxide.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct description of anaerobic glucose breakdown producing ethanol and carbon dioxide.

rubric.why: The balanced equation shows one glucose molecule producing two ethanol molecules and two carbon dioxide molecules.
rubric.description: Correct balanced equation for alcoholic fermentation.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the balanced equation: C6H12O6 → 2C2H5OH + 2CO2 (energy may also be shown).

modelAnswer: Alcoholic fermentation is the anaerobic breakdown of glucose, usually by yeast, into ethanol and carbon dioxide.

items.followUp: Write two functions of the liver other than producing bile.

rubric.why: The liver helps regulate blood glucose by storing glucose as glycogen and releasing glucose when needed.
rubric.description: Regulation of blood glucose or storage of glucose as glycogen.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for any correct liver function related to blood glucose regulation or glycogen storage.

rubric.why: The liver has several other functions, including detoxification, deamination, storage of vitamins, and breakdown of old red blood cells.
rubric.description: One other correct non-digestive function of the liver.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for any one correct function, such as detoxification, deamination, vitamin storage, or breakdown of old red blood cells.

modelAnswer: The liver regulates blood glucose by storing excess glucose as glycogen.
It detoxifies harmful substances in the blood.
